memory_update.text: Primary Layer 1B candidates for the enterprise agentic software/data/security node: NOW, CRM, PLTR, SNOW, MSFT.

The strongest investable mapping is not generic LLM access; it is ownership of workflow surfaces, enterprise data context, permissions, identity, auditability and governance needed to move AI agents into production.

Identity/security pure plays such as OKTA and CRWD showed relevant evidence for AI-agent identity, non-human identity governance and agentic SOC workflows, but were excluded due to the 5-candidate cap; they should be reviewed in a focused identity/security sub-pass.

Other plausible but lower-priority candidates for later passes include ORCL, ADBE, DDOG, MDB, ESTC, CFLT, PATH, TEAM, WORK-equivalent private/owned assets, and AI governance specialists; inclusion should depend on measurable AI revenue, paid adoption, and production deployment evidence.
Add NOW as a high-priority workflow-surface candidate for enterprise agentic software; evidence focus should be Now Assist ACV, agentic workflow adoption, and incremental AI monetization.
Add CRM as a high-priority systems-of-record and customer-workflow candidate; evidence focus should be Agentforce paid adoption and Data Cloud & AI ARR.

Keep PLTR in the node universe despite already appearing in the seed list because it maps directly to governed enterprise and government AI deployment through AIP and ontology-driven data integration.
Add SNOW as the governed enterprise-data-context supplier for AI agents; classify as inference because direct AI revenue attribution remains the key missing evidence.
Add OKTA as the non-human identity and AI-agent governance control-plane candidate; classify as hypothesis until dedicated AI-agent identity revenue or material attach-rate evidence appears.
Future passes should separately test observability/security operators such as DDOG, CRWD, PANW, ZS, and S as AI-agent monitoring, runtime security, and policy-enforcement suppliers.
Add ServiceNow (NOW), Salesforce (CRM), Snowflake (SNOW), Okta (OKTA), and Datadog (DDOG) as primary Layer 1B public-market candidates for the enterprise agentic software/data/security node.

For this node, the investable chokepoints cluster into four control layers: workflow surfaces, governed enterprise data context, identity/non-human identity governance, and production observability/security.

Workday (WDAY) has strong systems-of-record relevance through HR/finance workflows and an Agent System of Record, but was not included in the top-five candidate list because the pass prioritized broader cross-enterprise workflow, data, identity and observability coverage.

SailPoint (SAIL) and CyberArk exposure should be revisited in a dedicated identity-security pass. SailPoint is newly public again and directly targets agent identity security; CyberArk's standalone public mapping may be affected by Palo Alto Networks acquisition developments and should be verified before inclusion.

Palantir (PLTR), Microsoft (MSFT), Alphabet (GOOGL) and Amazon (AMZN) remain relevant to enterprise AI platforms and cloud-agent infrastructure but were not repeated here because they are already represented in the seed universe or belong partly to broader cloud/platform layers.

summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded universe for the enterprise agentic software/data/security node. The strongest direct public-company exposures are platforms already embedded in systems of record, workflow orchestration, enterprise data context, identity/governance, or regulated operational deployment. This pass prioritizes ServiceNow, Salesforce, Palantir, Snowflake, and Microsoft as above-$1B US-listed leaders with visible AI-agent productization or governance/control-plane relevance. No buy/sell view is implied. Expanded the universe around the software chokepoint where enterprise AI agents must connect to systems of record, governed data, identity, workflow permissions, audit trails, and observability before production deployment. The strongest candidates are not generic model providers; they control workflow surfaces, data context, access control, or operational telemetry. This pass favors US-listed companies with plausible direct exposure to enterprise agentic deployment and excludes hardware, power, and cloud infrastructure names covered by other funnel layers. Layer 1B expansion for the AI software chokepoint suggests the investable universe should extend beyond model providers and generic AI apps into vendors that own enterprise workflow surfaces, governed data context, identity controls, and production observability. The highest-relevance public mappings in this pass are ServiceNow and Salesforce for workflow/CRM agent surfaces, Snowflake for governed enterprise data context, Okta for agent/non-human identity control, and Datadog for AI-agent/LLM observability and security.
